identification.summary: MirrorFace is a China-linked cyber-espionage actor that mainly targets Japan. ESET first documented it in 2022, when it went after Japanese political entities ahead of an election [S2]. In January 2025, Japan's National Police Agency (NPA) and its national cybersecurity center publicly attributed a campaign to it that had run since 2019 and sought information on Japan's national security and advanced technology [S1][S9]. In 2024 it reached beyond Japan: ESET reported its first known European target (a Central European diplomatic institute) [S3], and Trend Micro reported targets in Taiwan and India [S4]. Its signature tools are LODEINFO and NOOPDOOR (which ESET calls HiddenFace), plus the revived ANEL backdoor [S3][S4][S5][S6].
identification.firstObserved: Japanese police: active since at least 2019 [S1]. Trend Micro: LODEINFO used exclusively by Earth Kasha since 2019 [S4]. Trend Micro's 2025 reporting says Earth Kasha has run espionage since at least 2017 [S7].
identification.notes: Trend Micro tracks the overlapping cluster as Earth Kasha [S4][S5][S7], and Security Affairs reports Japan's advisory as treating MirrorFace and Earth Kasha as the same group [S1]. Cybereason reports a related LODEINFO/NOOPDOOR intrusion set as 'Cuckoo Spear' and links it to APT10 [S8]. The encyclopedia maps APT10 to Microsoft's Purple Typhoon record. No source gathered gives a separate Microsoft name for MirrorFace, so it is kept as a related sub-cluster rather than merged. MITRE tracks the group as G1054 [S11].

attribution.sponsor: China-linked. Japan's NPA describes the campaigns as systematic cyberattacks linked to China [S1][S9]. No source gathered names a specific PRC ministry or unit for MirrorFace itself.
attribution.confidence: Government attribution: Japan's NPA and its national cybersecurity center publicly attributed the 2019-2024 campaigns to MirrorFace in January 2025 [S1][S9]. Vendor positions changed over time. In 2022 ESET tracked MirrorFace as a separate entity and said it could not link it to a known APT group despite speculation about APT10 [S2]. In March 2025, after observing the APT10-associated ANEL backdoor, ESET assessed MirrorFace as a subgroup under the APT10 umbrella and noted this aligned with Kaspersky and Cybereason [S3]. Trend Micro says Earth Kasha is believed to be part of the wider APT10 umbrella [S7].
attribution.basis: Japanese government advisory (reported through press coverage) [S1][S9]; shared exclusive tooling (LODEINFO, NOOPDOOR/HiddenFace) and reuse of ANEL, which was previously tied to APT10 [S3][S5][S6]; vendor telemetry from ESET, Trend Micro, JPCERT/CC and Cybereason [S2][S3][S4][S6][S8].

objectives: Espionage and theft of information. Japan's police say the goal was information on Japan's national security and advanced technology [S1][S9]. ESET describes the aim as espionage and exfiltrating files of interest [S2], and Trend Micro judged the primary motivation to be theft of victims' information and data [S4]. The 2022 targeting of a political party before the July 2022 House of Councillors election shows interest in Japanese domestic politics [S2].

sectors: Advanced technology, including aerospace, semiconductor and manufacturing [S4][S6][S9]
targeting.notes: JPCERT/CC says early targets were media, political organizations, think tanks and universities, and that the focus shifted to manufacturers and research institutions from 2023 [S6]. Trend Micro says the 2024 move back to spear-phishing reflects a shift from enterprise targets to individuals [S5].

capabilities.summary: Spear-phishing with malicious attachments and links, including OneDrive-hosted ZIP archives that contain macro-enabled droppers [S1][S5][S7]. In 2023 the group exploited internet-facing VPN and edge devices: Array AG (CVE-2023-28461), Proself (CVE-2023-45727), FortiOS/FortiProxy (CVE-2023-27997) and Citrix [S4][S6]. Its custom backdoors are LODEINFO, NOOPDOOR/HiddenFace (shellcode injected into legitimate processes, loaded through XML or DLL side-loading, with encrypted code stored in the registry) and ANEL (loaded by ANELLDR through DLL side-loading) [S3][S5][S6]. It also uses Cobalt Strike [S4]. Newer tradecraft includes a customized AsyncRAT run inside Windows Sandbox to evade security controls, abuse of Visual Studio Code remote tunnels [S3], an updated ANEL that can run Beacon Object Files in memory, and NOOPDOOR that uses DNS-over-HTTPS to hide C2 lookups [S7]. MITRE lists the group's software, including MirrorStealer, DOWNIISSA and NOOPLDR [S11].

campaigns.name: NPA Campaign A (2019-2023)
campaigns.summary: Spear-phishing with malware-laden attachments, using LODEINFO, against Japanese think tanks, government, politicians and media.

campaigns.name: Operation LiberalFace
campaigns.summary: ESET reports spear-phishing against members of a Japanese political party ahead of the July 2022 House of Councillors election, delivering espionage and credential-stealing malware.

campaigns.name: NPA Campaign B (Feb-Oct 2023)
campaigns.summary: Exploitation of Array Networks, Citrix and Fortinet internet-facing devices to deploy Cobalt Strike, LODEINFO and NOOPDOOR against Japanese technology and research organizations.

campaigns.name: Earth Kasha edge-device campaign (early 2023-early 2024)
campaigns.summary: Trend Micro reports exploitation of Array AG, Proself and FortiOS flaws against advanced-technology and government targets in Japan, Taiwan and India, deploying LODEINFO, NOOPDOOR and Cobalt Strike.

campaigns.name: Return of ANEL / NPA Campaign C
campaigns.summary: Spear-phishing emails with OneDrive links target individuals at political organizations, research institutions, think tanks and international-relations bodies in Japan, delivering the revived ANEL backdoor alongside NOOPDOOR.

campaigns.name: JPCERT/CC and Cybereason (Cuckoo Spear) disclosures
campaigns.summary: JPCERT/CC details MirrorFace NOOPDOOR and LODEINFO attacks on Japanese organizations, and Cybereason publishes related 'Cuckoo Spear' findings.

campaigns.name: Operation AkaiRyu
campaigns.summary: ESET reports Q2-Q3 2024 targeting of a Central European diplomatic institute with an Expo 2025 lure. The intrusion used ANEL, AsyncRAT in Windows Sandbox and VS Code tunnels. Published March 2025; first known European target.

campaigns.name: Japanese government public attribution
campaigns.summary: Japan's NPA and national cybersecurity center attribute the 2019-2024 campaigns to MirrorFace and publish its methods to warn potential victims.

campaigns.name: ROAMINGMOUSE / updated ANEL campaign
campaigns.summary: Trend Micro detects spear-phishing against government and public institutions in Taiwan and Japan. A ROAMINGMOUSE Excel dropper delivered an updated ANEL, and the campaign possibly used SharpHide to launch a second-stage NOOPDOOR backdoor.

diamond.adversary: China-linked espionage operators; ESET and Trend Micro now place the cluster under the APT10 umbrella [S1][S3][S7].
diamond.capability: LODEINFO, NOOPDOOR/HiddenFace, ANEL/ANELLDR, ROAMINGMOUSE, Cobalt Strike and customized AsyncRAT; DLL side-loading, Windows Sandbox abuse, VS Code tunnels and DNS-over-HTTPS [S3][S4][S5][S6][S7].
diamond.infrastructure: Free or compromised email accounts and OneDrive links for delivery [S5]; exploited VPN and edge devices as entry points [S4][S6]; VS Code remote tunnels for access [S3]; DoH-concealed C2 [S7].
diamond.victim: Japanese government, politicians, think tanks, media, academia and advanced-technology and manufacturing firms; government bodies in Taiwan; targets in India; a European diplomatic institute [S1][S3][S4][S6].
diamond.socioPolitical: Collection on Japan's national security, advanced technology and domestic politics, including targeting around the 2022 election and the Expo 2025 lure [S1][S2][S3].
diamond.technology: Internet-facing Array, Fortinet, Citrix and Proself appliances; Windows endpoints that allow DLL side-loading and have Windows Sandbox and VS Code available; cloud file-sharing (OneDrive) [S3][S4][S6][S7].

gaps: Primary documents could not be opened: WebFetch failed (DNS resolution errors) for the ESET WeLiveSecurity reports, the Trend Micro blogs, the JPCERT/CC blog, The Hacker News and The Register. Content comes from search-result summaries and press-release excerpts. The NPA/NISC advisory itself (Japanese-language) was not retrieved.
The name of the Japanese co-issuing agency differs across coverage (NISC versus 'NCSC'); verify against the official notice.

Microsoft naming: no source gathered gives a Microsoft name for MirrorFace. APT10 maps to Purple Typhoon elsewhere in this encyclopedia. Whether Microsoft tracks MirrorFace inside Purple Typhoon is unverified.
Cluster boundaries: MirrorFace (ESET, NPA), Earth Kasha (Trend Micro) and Cuckoo Spear (Cybereason) overlap but are not proven identical. ESET reversed its 2022 'separate entity' position in 2025.

Sector list attributed to the NPA advisory (aerospace, semiconductor, information and communications) comes from secondary coverage, and the attribution of each item to a specific outlet is approximate.
No public information on the sponsoring PRC organization, operator identities or any indictments specific to MirrorFace.
Victim outcomes, such as data stolen and the number of organizations compromised, are not public in the sources gathered.
IOCs (for example, IPs republished by third parties for the 2024 ANEL campaign) were not verified against Trend Micro originals.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: The operational environment includes allied Japanese government, political, think-tank and defense-industrial networks, Taiwanese government institutions, and diplomatic bodies that engage on Japan [S1][S3][S7]. Internet-facing VPN appliances and personal or cloud email are key terrain [S4][S5]. STEP 2: Patches to edge devices (Array, Fortinet, Citrix) and controls on Windows Sandbox, VS Code tunnels and DoH egress shape the actor's access [S3][S4][S7]. STEP 3: The model runs from a tailored spear-phish (OneDrive ZIP, macro document, event-themed lure) or an edge-device exploit, to DLL side-loaded ANEL, LODEINFO or NOOPDOOR, to credential theft and file exfiltration [S3][S5][S6][S7]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued spear-phishing of individuals in Japan- and Taiwan-related policy, research and diplomatic communities to collect security and technology information [S1][S5][S7]. MDCOA is exploitation of edge devices at defense-industrial or coalition partners, establishing durable NOOPDOOR access that harvests alliance planning or advanced-technology data during a regional crisis [S4][S6]. Candidate indicators: unexpected VS Code tunnel processes or code.exe network sessions; Windows Sandbox (.wsb) launched on non-developer hosts; signed binaries side-loading unknown DLLs; encrypted blobs in the registry; DoH traffic from endpoints; OneDrive-delivered ZIPs with macro-enabled Excel files [S3][S6][S7].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track Japanese government (NPA) and JPCERT/CC advisories alongside vendor reporting, because allied disclosures preceded or complemented vendor reporting [S1][S6]. (2) Authorities: the actor targets allied and partner networks (Japan, Taiwan, European diplomatic bodies), so most response actions sit with host nations; DoD action centers on its own networks and information sharing [S1][S3][S7]. (3) Mission assurance: harden and monitor internet-facing VPN appliances on DODIN and Defense Industrial Base enclaves that support Indo-Pacific operations, and restrict VS Code tunnels and Windows Sandbox where not required [S3][S4]. (4) Coordination: share indicators with Japanese counterparts, USINDOPACOM components and DC3/DIB partners, and deconflict naming (MirrorFace, Earth Kasha, APT10/Purple Typhoon) in shared reporting [S1][S3][S7].
